record.title: Dowling geometry Kinser-inequality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let a **Dowling geometry** be the matroid constructed from the corresponding labelled graph whose circuits are the positive cycles and minimal connected subgraphs containing two negative cycles. A Kinser inequality is the rank inequality indexed by an integer $n\geq 4$. **Dowling geometry Kinser-inequality conjecture.** A Dowling geometry satisfies every Kinser inequality.

The source notes that this is open when $G$ is finite and non-cyclic; finite subgroups of the multiplicative group of a field are cyclic, so the representable cases do not settle the non-cyclic case.
record.source_name: Amanda Cameron, “Kinser inequalities and related matroids”, arXiv:1401.0500 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Skew partial-field Kinser-inequality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}=(R,G)$ be a skew partial field, and let $M$ be a matroid that is **$\mathbb{P}$-representable**, meaning that it arises from a $\mathbb{P}$-chain group as in the source. A Kinser inequality is the rank inequality indexed by an integer $n\geq 4$. **Skew partial-field Kinser-inequality conjecture.** If $M$ is $\mathbb{P}$-representable, then $M$ satisfies every Kinser inequality.

The claim would extend the known fact that ordinary representable matroids satisfy all Kinser inequalities to matroids representable over skew partial fields. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Amanda Cameron, “Kinser inequalities and related matroids”, arXiv:1401.0500 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Monomial equivalence of two six-dimensional toric codes over the field with eight elements
record.statement: Let $P_6^{(4)}$ and $P_6^{(5)}$ be the polytopes indexing the corresponding six-dimensional toric codes $C_{P_6^{(4)}}$ and $C_{P_6^{(5)}}$ over $\mathbb{F}_8$. **The conjecture.** The codes $C_{P_6^{(4)}}$ and $C_{P_6^{(5)}}$ over $\mathbb{F}_8$ are monomially equivalent. The preceding classification establishes this equivalence in all other relevant cases except that this particular equivalence remains open; the conjecture is motivated by the fact that the two codes have exactly the same enumerator polynomial.
record.source_name: Xue Luo, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Mingyi Zhang and Huaiqing Zuo, “On Classification of Toric Surface Codes of Low Dimension”, arXiv:1402.0060 (2014).
record.references:

record.title: Regularity conjecture for weakly closed graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected weakly closed graph, let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]$, and let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal. Let $\ell$ denote the length of the longest induced path of $G$. **Regularity conjecture for weakly closed graphs.** If the longest induced path of $G$ has length $\ell$, then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/J_G)=\ell.
$$

The claim extends the corresponding result for connected closed graphs and the authors establish it for trees, where the relevant graphs are precisely caterpillar trees; the supplied text reports that the general weakly closed-graph case is motivated by computer experiments and leaves it as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Faryal Chaudhry, Ahmet Dokuyucu and Rida Irfan, “On the binomial edge ideals of block graphs”, arXiv:1402.2041 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2041

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: Conjecture on small sumsets of iterated product sets
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of real numbers, and let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. Define

$$
A^{(k)}:=\{a_1\cdots a_k:a_1,\ldots,a_k\in A\}.
$$

**Iterated product-set sum conjecture.** The $k$-fold sumset of $A^{(k)}$ should satisfy

$$
|kA^{(k)}|\gg |A|^k.
$$

The preceding theorem proves the weaker bound with $4^{k-1}$ summands instead of $k$ summands. The conjecture asks whether the number of summands can be reduced to $k$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Antal Balog and Oliver Roche-Newton, “New sum-product estimates for real and complex numbers”, arXiv:1402.5775 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.5775

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The Graßmann-Tamari lattice conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_{k,n}$ denote the Graßmann-Tamari poset on the relevant Graßmannian tableaux. The usual Tamari order is recovered when $k=2$. **Graßmann-Tamari lattice conjecture.** For general $k$, the Graßmann-Tamari poset $\mathcal{T}_{k,n}$ is a lattice. The conjecture is motivated by the self-dual lattice structure of the ordinary Tamari order and was tested in the source for $k=3$ and $n\in\{6,7,8\}$; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Francisco Santos, Christian Stump and Volkmar Welker, “Noncrossing sets and a Graßmann associahedron”, arXiv:1403.8133 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.8133

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2014).

record.title: Distinct prefix normal words have distinct extension-count sequences
record.statement:
Let $v,w
e 0$ be distinct prefix normal binary words, with extension counts $\textit{ext}(v,m)$ and $\textit{ext}(w,m)$ denoting the numbers of prefix normal extensions of length $m$. **Distinct-extension-sequence conjecture.** If $v\neq w$, then the infinite sequences

$$
(\textit{ext}(v,m))_{m\geq 1}\quad\text{and}\quad(\textit{ext}(w,m))_{m\geq 1}
$$

are different. The preceding lemma establishes the analogous claim for the extension languages themselves, but the paper does not prove that their growth sequences differ.
record.source_name: Péter Burcsi, Gabriele Fici, Zsuzsanna Lipták, Frank Ruskey and Joe Sawada, “Normal, Abby Normal, Prefix Normal”, arXiv:1404.2824 (2014).
record.references:

record.title: A lower-bound conjecture for the regularity of long linear equations
record.statement:
For a positive integer $r$, let an equation be **$r$-regular** when every coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors has a monochromatic positive-integer solution. **Lower-bound conjecture.** For each positive integer $r$, there is an integer $n(r)$ such that, whenever $n\geq n(r)$, every linear homogeneous equation in $n$ variables with nonzero integer coefficients not all of the same sign is $r$-regular.
This asserts a nontrivial uniform lower bound on the degree of regularity for sufficiently long equations. The supplied text presents it as an apparent conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Noah Golowich, “Resolving a Conjecture on Degree of Regularity of Linear Homogeneous Equations”, arXiv:1404.3384 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.3384

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2014).

record.title: Manoussakis's degree-sum conjecture for Hamilton cycles in digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a strongly 2-connected digraph on $n$ vertices. For vertices $x,y,w,z$, call each pair **nonadjacent** when neither corresponding arc is present.

**Manoussakis's conjecture.** If $x,y$ and $w,z$ are distinct pairs of nonadjacent vertices and

$$
d(x)+d(y)+d(w)+d(z)\geq 4n-3,
$$

then $D$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture proposes a degree-sum condition extending Manoussakis's earlier Hamiltonicity theorem. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Bo Ning, “Notes on a conjecture of Manoussakis concerning Hamilton cycles in digraphs”, arXiv:1404.5013 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.5013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2014).

record.title: Pikhurko–Zhao Motzkin–Straus conjecture for hypergraphs without a large clique
record.statement:
Let $t$, $m$, and $r\geq 3$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\binom{t-1}{r}\leq m\leq \binom{t-1}{r}+\binom{t-2}{r-1}.
$$

Let $G$ be an $r$-graph with $m$ edges that does not contain a clique of order $t-1$.

**Pikhurko–Zhao conjecture.** The Lagrangian of $G$ satisfies

$$
\lambda(G)<\lambda([t-1]^{(r)}).
$$

This complements the corresponding clique-containing assertion and gives a strict Lagrangian bound in the same edge range. The source presents it as a conjecture; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Qingsong Tang, Xiaojun Lu, Xiangde Zhang and Cheng Zhao, “On hypergraph Lagrangians”, arXiv:1405.2855 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2855

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: Regularity-preserving orientations for quivers with loop underlying graph
record.statement: Let $Q$ be a quiver whose underlying graph is a loop, and let $\operatorname{Rep}_k(Q)$ denote its category of representations over $k$. A category is **regularity preserving** when it has the regularity-preservation property studied in the source. **Regularity-preserving orientation conjecture.** For each quiver $Q$ whose underlying graph is a loop, there is a choice of orientation of the arrows such that $\operatorname{Rep}_k(Q)$ is regularity preserving. The source presents this as an example of a broader unexplored picture beyond the known regularity-preserving examples, so the asserted existence of suitable orientations remains open.
record.source_name: George Dimitrov and Ludmil Katzarkov, “Non-semistable exceptional objects in hereditary categories: some remarks and conjectures”, arXiv:1405.2943 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2943

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: The linear formula for vertex Folkman numbers with parameters 3 and p
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an integer and, for $r\geq1$, let $F_v(2_r,3,p;r+p+1)$ denote the vertex Folkman number with $r$ entries equal to $2$, together with parameters $3$ and $p$. **The $(2_r,3,p)$ Folkman conjecture.** If $p\geq4$, then

$$
\min\left\{F_v(2_r,3,p;r+p-1)-r\right\}=F_v(3,p;p+1),
$$

and therefore

$$
F_v(2_r,3,p;r+p+1)=F_v(3,p;p+1)+r.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the computed values $r”_0(4)=r”_0(5)=0$ and would give an explicit formula for this family of vertex Folkman numbers. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Aleksandar Bikov and Nedyalko Nenov, “On the vertex Folkman numbers F_v(a_1, ..., a_s; m - 1) when \a_1, ..., a_s\ = 6 or 7”, arXiv:1512.02051 (2017).

record.title: Fermionic reformulation of dispersive universal Whitham hierarchies
record.statement: Let $C$ be any spectral curve, and let the dispersive universal Whitham integrable hierarchy associated with $C$ be the corresponding hierarchy. **Fermionic reformulation conjecture.** There is a fermionic reformulation of dispersive universal Witham integrable hierarchy associated with any spectral curve. The conjecture extends fermionic descriptions known for special cases of partition functions and is intended to relate dispersive universal Whitham hierarchies to fermionic formalisms; the source mentions partial results but no general proof.

record.title: The alternating-group generation conjecture for Toffoli gates
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet of even order, let $n\geq3$, let $S_A$ be the symmetric group on $A$, and let $TG(i,\alpha,o)$ denote the $i$-ary Toffoli gate with permutation $\alpha\in S_A$ and control value $o\in A$. Let $B_n$ be the group of invertible maps on $A^n$. **Alternating-group generation conjecture.** The set

$$
\\{TG(i,\alpha,o)\mid \alpha\in S_A,\\ i<n,\\ o\in A\\}
$$

should generate a subgroup of $B_n$ isomorphic to the alternating group on $A^n$, except when $|A|=2$ and $n=3$. The claim is based on examples computed in GAP; the exceptional case is explicitly excluded, and no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Tim Boykett, “Closed Systems of Invertible Maps”, arXiv:1512.06813 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Dunfield–Gukov–Rasmussen spectral sequence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot. Its HOMFLY-PT homology and knot Floer homology are homological invariants associated to $K$.

**Dunfield–Gukov–Rasmussen conjecture.** There is a spectral sequence from HOMFLY-PT homology to knot Floer homology.

This conjecture proposes a direct relationship between two knot homology theories. The paper develops such a relationship using the oriented cube of resolutions and proves results supporting the existence of a spectral sequence whose higher pages are link invariants and which converges to knot Floer homology.
record.source_name: Nathan Dowlin, “A Categorification of the HOMFLY-PT Polynomial with a Spectral Sequence to Knot Floer Homology”, arXiv:1703.01401 (2017).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1511.08953](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.08953).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.01401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

record.title: The strong conciseness conjecture for profinite groups
record.statement: Let $w(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ be a word in $k$ variables, and let $G$ be a profinite group. Write $w\{G\}$ for the set of word-values of $w$ in $G$, and $w(G)=\langle w\{G\}\rangle$ for the verbal subgroup. A word is **strongly concise** in $G$ if $|w\{G\}|<2^{\aleph_0}$ implies that $w(G)$ is finite. **Strong conciseness conjecture.** Every word is strongly concise in the class of profinite groups. This strengthens ordinary conciseness by replacing finiteness of the word-value set with cardinality strictly below the continuum; the supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Andoni Zozaya, “Conciseness of compact R-analytic groups”, arXiv:2202.01266 (2023).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.01344](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01344), [arXiv:1507.03362](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03362).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01266

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2022). “Nevertheless, as Jaikin-Zapirain highlighted in , P. Hall's conjecture is still open for profinite groups: Every word is concise in the class of profinite groups.”

record.title: Order bounds for 2K2-split minimal (∞, k)-polar obstructions
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\ge 3$, and let $G=(C,S,I)$ be a $2K_2$-split minimal $(\infty,k)$-polar obstruction. Write $c=|C|$ and $i=|I|$ for the numbers of vertices in $C$ and $I$, respectively.

**Order-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
k\le i\le 2k-2\quad\text{and}\quad c\le 2k-i-1.
$$

This conjecture gives sharper structural bounds on the clique and independent-set parts of minimal $(\infty,k)$-polar obstructions and could help establish improved bounds on their order. The source presents it as an initial conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: F. Esteban Contreras Mendoza and César Hernández Cruz, “Polarity on H-split graphs”, arXiv:2303.17055 (2023).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2104.07852](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07852), [arXiv:1511.09429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.09429).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: Twin-free reduction conjecture for $(3+1)$-free posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a $(3+1)$-free poset, meaning that it contains no induced subposet isomorphic to the disjoint union of a $3$-chain and a $1$-chain. Call $P$ **twin-free** when there is no graph $G$ with a vertex $v$ such that $\operatorname{Inc}(P)=G_v$, where $G_v$ is obtained by twinning $G$ at $v$.

**Twin-free reduction conjecture.** If $P$ is $(3+1)$-free and twin-free, then $X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P)}(\mathbf{x})$ is $e$-positive.

The source says that, if the preceding $(3+1)$-free twinning conjecture is solved, the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture can be reduced to this conjecture. Its independent resolution status is not given.
record.source_name: Esther Banaian, Kyle Celano, Megan Chang-Lee, Laura Colmenarejo, Owen Goff, Jamie Kimble, Lauren Kimpel, John Lentfer, Jinting Liang and Sheila Sundaram, “The e-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function for twinned paths and cycles”, arXiv:2405.17649 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1504.06257](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06257).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17649

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2024). “A counterexample to this conjecture was given by Li, Li, Wang, and Yang (2021).”

record.title: Neumann–Lara's acyclic 2-coloring conjecture for planar digraphs
record.statement:
A digraph is a directed graph, and an **acyclic set** is a vertex set inducing no directed cycle. A vertex-partition into two acyclic sets is a partition of all vertices into two such sets.

**Neumann–Lara's conjecture.** Every planar digraph of digirth at least $3$ can be vertex-partitioned into two acyclic sets.

The source states that this conjecture remains open in general, although Li and Mohar established it for planar digraphs of digirth at least $4$.
record.source_name: Simon Dreyer, Alexandre Pinlou and Petru Valicov, “Feedback vertex sets of planar digraphs with fixed digirth”, arXiv:2605.12279 (2026).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1712.06143](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06143), [arXiv:1504.06726](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06726).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12279

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “While remains open in general, it was established by Li and Mohar for planar digraphs of digirth at least 4.”

record.title: Lescure–Meyniel conjecture for strong immersions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $K_{chi(G)}$ be the complete graph on $chi(G)$ vertices. A **strong immersion** of a graph $H$ in $G$ consists of an injection from $V(H)$ to $V(G)$ and pairwise edge-disjoint paths representing the edges of $H$, whose internal vertices avoid the image of the injection. **Lescure–Meyniel conjecture.** Every graph $G$ contains a strong immersion of $K_{chi(G)}$. This is the strong-immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture. It implies the Abu-Khzam–Langston conjecture for weak immersions, and both conjectures remain open in general; the statement is known for chromatic number at most $7$.
record.source_name: Jonathan C. Dahlke, “The Abu-Khzamx2013Langston Conjecture for Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2605.28159 (2026).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2510.05893](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05893), [arXiv:1512.00513](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00513), [arXiv:1502.01786](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01786).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28159

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Since every strong immersion is a weak immersion, clearly implies ; both remain open in general.”
